cover.headline: You pay for the core and get the stakes free: a cheap, cash-rich leader whose home market is shrinking
cover.lead: Hero MotoCorp is the world's largest two-wheeler maker (64.69 lakh units in FY26) and owns India's 100-110cc motorcycle market (~96% of it). That segment is losing ground: commuter motorcycles fell from 42% to 32% of industry volume in five years and Hero's overall share from 31% to 23%. The GST cut of Sep-2025 and fast gains in scooters, 125cc and VIDA electric scooters lifted Q1FY27 volume 23% and revenue 36%, but August dispatches rose only 2.7%, commodity costs cut the margin to 13.3% and the 2026 monsoon ended ~13% short. Hero also owns ~32% of Ather Energy (worth ~₹18,458 cr at the 30-Sep close) and 40% of Hero FinCorp. The street values it on **P/E on FY28E core EPS (16-18x) plus the stakes**. We do the same: **15x Sep-28E EPS of ₹349.4 (₹5,241) plus ₹868 a share for the stakes** gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}})**: **we initiate with BUY.** Cross-checks: EV/EBITDA ₹5,359, DCF ₹7,399. Bull {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: The core is priced like a business in decline
arguments.p: Take out the stakes (₹868 a share after a 20% discount) and ₹5,241 buys the core at 13.3x our FY28E EPS, against a 16.4x median forward multiple since 2021 on the same basis. Our 15x already includes the 7% de-rating of auto stocks.

Record share in 100-110cc (96%), 125cc back to 18%, ICE scooters doubled to 7%, VIDA ~11% of e-scooters, parts +30% in Q1FY27, exports up 39% in FY26. 35% ROCE, negative working capital and a 70% payout (~4% yield at our FY28E DPS).

arguments.h: But growth is modest and fragile
arguments.p: We forecast volume +{{as.volume.growth.0|n1}}% in FY27E and ~5% a year after; EPS ~9% a year to FY29E. H2FY27 laps the post-GST surge, the monsoon was the weakest since 2015 and TVS out-sold Hero in August. The EV shift erodes the 100cc moat over time.

arguments.h: Ather is a big, volatile part of the value
arguments.p: Ather is ~₹734 a share of our target (12%) after a 20% discount; at ~15x trailing sales it can move 30% either way. Every ₹100 on Ather's price is ~₹50 on our target. Hero FinCorp (₹95) made a loss in FY26.

catalysts: Festive season (Navratri to Diwali falls in Oct-Nov 2026, later than 2025) and Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): whether retail holds up after a weak monsoon, and the margin after Q2's "marginal uptick" in input costs.
Monthly dispatches: August was +2.7% with exports -24.5%; motorcycles need to grow again against the post-GST base from October.
VIDA: capacity from ~30k to ~45k a month by Q4FY27, PLI on 100% of the range by Dec-2026, EBITDA-breakeven ambition by year-end.
Premium launches over the next 12 months (new premium business head from Aug-2026); Harley-Davidson range.
Ather: share price, conversion of the 76.19 lakh warrants (₹720 cr due within 18 months) and its own results; Hero FinCorp IPO, which SEBI approved in 2025 but which had not launched by Sep-2026.

sections.title: What Hero does: 65 lakh two-wheelers a year, three-quarters of them 100cc-class commuter bikes

blocks.p: Hero designs, makes and sells motorcycles and scooters, and the spare parts for the ~130 million Hero vehicles sold since 1984. FY26 consolidated revenue was ₹47,411 cr: ₹39,085 cr from vehicles (82%), ₹6,592 cr from spare parts (14%) and ₹1,734 cr from services and export incentives. It has six plants in India plus Colombia and Bangladesh, ~8.63 mn units of capacity and 14,000+ customer touchpoints, with a point of sale in 93% of India's talukas. The parent company (standalone) is ~99% of the group; subsidiaries in Colombia, Bangladesh, the US and a German R&D centre added ~₹580 cr of revenue in FY26.

Volume is concentrated in one product family. Of 64.7 lakh units in FY26, 59% were 100-110cc Splendor and Passion motorcycles, 16% entry HF Deluxe, 10% 125cc (Glamour, Super Splendor, Xtreme 125R), 1% premium (>125cc: Xtreme 160R/250R, Xpulse, Karizma, Mavrick, Harley-Davidson X440), 7% ICE scooters, 2% VIDA electric scooters and 6% exports to 53 countries.

blocks.callout: **So what:** Hero is a 100-110cc motorcycle company with a large, very profitable parts business. That product is cheap (₹56,000-80,000 ex-showroom), fuel-efficient and bought mainly by rural and first-time buyers. Hero's fortunes therefore follow farm incomes, fuel prices and the price gap between a motorcycle and the alternatives, and its growth depends on segments where it is still small: scooters, EVs, 125cc and premium.

blocks.p: Two things stand out. First, Hero lost share for a decade after Honda left in 2011: domestic share fell from ~37% in FY21 to ~27% now, as Honda, TVS and Bajaj won scooters, 125cc and premium buyers while Hero stayed with 100cc commuters. Second, Hero has been an investor more than a builder in new technology: it backed Ather from 2016 and launched its own VIDA only in 2022. The Ather bet has paid off on paper (₹1,425 a share at 30-Sep-2026 against an IPO price of ₹321); VIDA is now growing fast but still loses ~₹230 cr a quarter.

blocks.callout: **Leadership churn:** three CEOs in five years (Niranjan Gupta from May-2023 to Apr-2025, Vikram Kasbekar acting, Harshavardhan Chitale from Jan-2026), new heads for EV (2025), technology (May-2026) and premium (Aug-2026). The new team has delivered share gains in scooters and EVs within nine months, but it is too early to judge the strategy.

blocks.p: Three forces matter for Hero. **Affordability**: the GST cut lowered the price of a Splendor by ~₹6,800 and lifted festive 2025 retail; Hero's VAHAN share hit 31.6% in Oct-2025. But price increases since February 2026 (~4.5% blended) and the weak monsoon now work the other way. **Mix**: buyers are moving to scooters (31.5% of the market), 125cc and premium bikes, and exports (21%), where Hero is small. **Electrification**: e-scooters were 11.2% of retail in July 2026; commuter motorcycles are not yet electrifying (no product, use case of long rural rides, heavy loads), which protects Hero's core for now. Management expects FY27 industry growth to approach double digits.

blocks.callout: **So what:** the industry is growing faster than at any time since FY19, but the growth is in the parts of the market where Hero is weakest. Hero's share of the total (including exports) slid from 31% in FY21 to 23% in Q1FY27 even as its volumes hit records.

blocks.title: Does the sector tailwind reach Hero?
blocks.source: SIAM/VAHAN via Emkay; company calls; IMD

blocks.callout: **Verdict:** Hero gets the volume tailwind (tax cut, demand recovery) because it owns the entry market, but not the mix tailwind (premium, scooters, exports) that lifts realisations and margins for peers. That is a large part of why Hero trades at ~19x trailing earnings while Eicher, TVS and Bajaj trade at 25-48x.

sections.title: Commuter motorcycles: a near-monopoly in a segment that is losing share of the market

blocks.p: Hero sold 54.2 lakh entry, deluxe and 125cc motorcycles in India in FY26, ~84% of its volume and, we estimate, ~65% of revenue. In 100-110cc (Splendor, Passion) its share rose from 87% in FY21 to 96.4% in Q1FY27: nine of ten buyers choose Hero for mileage, reliability and resale value. In Q1FY27 deluxe volume grew 20.5%, Splendor 15% and 125cc 45% (share back to 17.7% from 12.8% a year earlier on Glamour X and Xtreme 125R), while entry HF Deluxe fell 19% as buyers traded up after the GST cut. Hero added 2,000 units a day of Splendor capacity in Q1FY27 and launched E20-E85 flex-fuel Splendor and HF Deluxe versions in July.

pair.title: 100-110cc share at a record 96%; 125cc recovering
pair.unit: Hero share of domestic segment, SIAM (%)

pair.title: Domestic motorcycles: 43 lakh (FY22, Covid-hit) to 55 lakh

blocks.p: The problem is the segment, not Hero's position in it. Commuter motorcycles were 42% of industry volume in FY21 and 32% in Q1FY27, as rising incomes push buyers to scooters, 125cc and premium bikes and as women and urban buyers choose scooters. Entry (economy) bikes have shrunk to 5% of the market. Price increases since February 2026 (~4.5%) and higher fuel prices test affordability; Hero cut the price of one HF Deluxe variant in some states in July to pull first-time buyers back. Electrification is not an immediate threat here (no affordable electric commuter bike yet, long rural rides, heavy loads), but Hero itself plans electric motorcycles from FY28.

blocks.callout: **So what:** this is the cash engine. We assume deluxe volume +8% in FY27E (Q1 strength, then a high post-GST base and a weak monsoon) and 3-4% after, 125cc +7-15%, and entry bikes shrinking 5-12% a year. Net realisation rises with the ~5% price increases already taken. The risk is the rural cycle: the 2026 monsoon ended ~13% short, and the entry and deluxe buyer is the first to delay a purchase.

sections.title: Scooters and VIDA: growing fast from far behind; VIDA still loses ~₹230 cr a quarter

blocks.p: Scooters are 31.5% of the market and Hero's share was only 4.6% (ICE) in Q1FY26. Since then Destini 125 and the Xoom range lifted ICE scooter dispatches 84% in Q1FY27 (share 6.9%); Destini capacity has been doubled and Xoom raised 50%, with channel stock at half the normal level. In electric scooters VIDA's VAHAN registrations rose from 18,783 (FY24) to 50,800 (FY25) and 1,49,341 (FY26); Q1FY27 dispatches were 56,837 (+151%) and retail is now >20,000 a month (~11% share, #4 behind TVS, Bajaj and Ather). The low-cost VX2 with battery-as-a-service (from ₹0.9 a km) and removable batteries drove the jump; Hero was also less hit than rivals by the 2025 rare-earth magnet shortage.

pair.title: Share gains in both ICE and electric scooters
VIDA retail: 19k a year to 1.5 lakh in two years

blocks.p: VIDA is still a cost centre. Management puts the "P&L investment" at ~₹220 cr in Q4FY26 and ~₹230 cr in Q1FY27, a 2.4-2.6 point drag on group margin; the EBITDA loss per unit fell from ~₹50,000 to ~₹40,000. EV revenue was ~₹660 cr in Q1FY27 (5% of revenue). Three levers: PLI (₹48 cr accrued in Q1FY27 on 60% of the range; ~13% of EV revenue once the whole range qualifies by Dec-2026), scale (capacity ~30k a month from August, ~45k by Q4FY27) and cost reduction; some models are already gross-margin positive and management aims for breakeven "by the end of the year". Electric motorcycles (Ubex, VXZ with Zero Motorcycles) come only from FY28.

blocks.callout: **So what:** Hero has gone from irrelevant to credible in scooters within a year, helped by capacity it now has. But it is a follower: TVS, Bajaj and Ather each sell more e-scooters, and Hero owns a third of Ather, its competitor. We model VIDA at ~2.8 lakh units in FY27E and losses narrowing to ~₹900 cr for the year, inside our 13.7% group margin.

sections.title: Premium, exports and parts: parts is the hidden gem; premium remains a gap

blocks.p: **Premium (>125cc)** is the most profitable part of the market (13.5% of industry volume) and Hero's weakest: 71,320 units in FY26 and a 1.5% share in Q1FY27, down from 3.8% in FY21. The Harley-Davidson X440 range (made by Hero) grew 26% in FY26, helped by the new X440T variant; the Xtreme 250R and Mavrick 440 did not move share. A new premium head (ex-Royal Enfield) took over in Aug-2026 with "many" launches promised over 12 months. **Exports** (4.0 lakh units, ~₹3,500 cr in FY26) grew ~40% a year in FY25-26 and 63% in Q1FY27, then fell 14% in July and 24.5% in August 2026. Hero entered Germany and Ecuador in 2026; Colombia, Bangladesh and Nepal are the core markets.

**Parts, accessories and merchandise (PAM)** earned ₹6,592 cr in FY26 (AR, consolidated; ~₹6,200 cr per management), 14% of revenue, and grew 30% in Q1FY27 (₹1,689 cr) and ~25% in July. Management estimates that about half of Hero-parts demand is still met by the grey market; the ₹750 cr second parts centre at Tirupati (foundation stone 1-Jul-2026, commissioning by end-2027) more than doubles capacity. Parts carry well above-average margins, which is why ICE margins held at 15.9% despite the commodity hit.

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** Hero has a real moat, but a narrow one. In 100-110cc motorcycles its brand, rural reach, service network, resale values and scale give it ~96% of the segment and the lowest cost per unit in the industry; nobody has dented that in 15 years. Outside that segment it has no structural advantage: in scooters, premium bikes, exports and EVs it is a late, small challenger that wins share only when it out-spends and out-launches rivals. Because its core segment is shrinking as a share of the market, the moat protects cash flow, not growth.

sections.title: A decade of slow growth, then FY26: record volumes after the GST cut

blocks.p: Hero's consolidated revenue grew from ₹28,457 cr in FY16 to ₹47,411 cr in FY26, only 5.2% a year, and profit from ₹3,112 cr to ₹5,776 cr (6.4% a year). For most of the decade volumes went nowhere: a new emission standard (BS6, Apr-2020), Covid and a rural slowdown pushed revenue down to ₹29,551 cr in FY22. The recovery since then has come in three steps: price increases and a better mix (FY23-24, EBITDA margin from 11% to 14%), a steady FY25 (+8%) and the September-2025 GST cut, which lifted FY26 volumes 9.6% to 64.69 lakh and revenue 16%. Note that reported FY26 profit includes a one-time ₹722 cr gain from the dilution of Hero's stake in its associates (Ather's IPO and a private placement): before associates and one-offs, FY26 EPS was ~₹283, not ₹287.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** Hero is a mature, cash-rich business whose growth depends on rural incomes and the price of a 100cc motorcycle. FY26 was helped by a one-off tax cut; FY27 by price increases. The margin recovery since FY22 is real (price discipline, cost programme "LEAP", parts), but the EV build-out costs ~2.3-2.6 points of margin and commodity costs turned up again in 2026. We do not expect the 15%+ margins of FY16-18 while VIDA is loss-making.

sections.title: Returns back to the mid-30s; most cash goes out as dividends, a growing slice into stakes

blocks.p: Hero needs little capital: capex was ₹2,745 cr over FY24-26 against ₹17,535 cr of operating cash flow. ROCE fell from ~50% in FY15-16 to 18% in FY22 (low volumes, BS6 costs) and is back at 35% in FY26. Dividends took ₹9,009 cr over FY24-26; investments in group companies and start-ups (Ather, Euler Motors, Zero Motorcycles) ₹1,483 cr. In FY27 the pattern changes: ₹1,998 cr went into Ather in August-2026 alone (₹1,758 cr of shares from GIC plus 25% of ₹960 cr of warrants), with ₹720 cr more due if the warrants are converted, and capex rises to the guided ₹1,500 cr.

blocks.callout: **The capital question:** Hero pays out 70%+ of profit and still adds to cash. The debate is the use of the rest. Management has chosen to own a third of Ather (₹2,700 cr committed in 2026 at ₹1,260-1,480 a share) while also building VIDA, and to fund Hero FinCorp (which lost ₹226 cr in FY26). The Ather stake has been a good investment so far; Hero FinCorp has not.

sections.title: Earnings quality: clean and cash-backed, but reported profit mixes in associates and one-offs

bullets: **Cash backs profit.** Operating cash flow was 144% of reported profit in FY26 (₹2,375 cr working-capital inflow as payables rose), 98% in FY25 and 132% in FY24; over FY15-26 cash from operations (₹46,845 cr) exceeded profit (₹41,828 cr).

**Associates sit inside consolidated profit.** Hero equity-accounts Hero FinCorp, Ather and Euler: their share of profit/loss was −₹120 cr (FY24), −₹161 cr (FY25) and +₹385 cr (FY26, including a ₹722 cr gain when Ather's IPO and a private placement diluted Hero's stake). Excluding them and the one-offs, FY26 EPS was ~₹283, not the reported ₹287. Our forecasts exclude associates and value the stakes separately.

**Other income is sizeable and volatile.** ₹1,058 cr in FY26 (consolidated, 14% of pre-tax profit): ₹293 cr interest, ₹128 cr gains on sale and ₹533 cr fair-value gains on debt funds, net of a ₹222 cr write-down of the Zero Motorcycles stake after a dilutive round. Mark-to-market gains rise and fall with bond yields.
**One-offs:** ₹119 cr labour-code charge (FY26), ₹160 cr VRS (FY24). Small.

**Minorities and share count.** Screener's FY26 "Net Profit" (₹5,776 cr) is before ₹34 cr of minorities; EPS uses ₹5,742 cr. The engine's implied share count (20.13 cr) is 0.6% above the actual 20.01 cr; below our 1% threshold, so no adjustment.

**Tax:** an income-tax demand from a 2022 search (₹178 cr in FY25, ₹27 cr outstanding) is under appeal with no provision; PLI incentives are booked as income (₹48 cr in Q1FY27, growing as the whole VIDA range qualifies).

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: GREEN.** Unqualified audit, strong cash conversion, negative working capital and a simple balance sheet. Two things to adjust for: associates (including one-off dilution gains) in consolidated profit, and mark-to-market treasury income. We strip out the first and normalise the second.

sections.title: The stakes: ~₹868 a share after a 20% discount, over 80% of it in Ather

blocks.p: Hero owns three large minority stakes, all **equity-accounted**: the consolidated accounts carry them at cost plus Hero's share of their profits or losses (₹3,901 cr at Mar-2026: Hero FinCorp ₹2,407 cr, Ather ₹1,093 cr, Euler ₹401 cr), and one line in the P&L, "share of profit/loss of associates", carries Hero's share of their results: +₹385 cr in FY26 (Hero FinCorp +₹70 cr, Ather +₹461 cr including the ₹722 cr dilution gain, Euler −₹109 cr) and −₹44 cr in Q1FY27. Book value says nothing about what the stakes are worth, and the P&L line is mostly noise (Ather's losses, one-off gains). So, like the street, we take them out of EPS and value them separately at the 30-Sep-2026 market price or on book.

blocks.p: **Ather Energy.** Hero has backed Ather since 2016 and owned 39.6% before its May-2025 IPO at ₹321; the IPO and later issues diluted it to 30.07% (Mar-2026) and 29.48% (Jun-2026). In 2026 Hero bought back in: 76.19 lakh warrants at ₹1,260 (₹960 cr, 25% paid, allotted 25-Aug-2026) and 1.188 cr shares from GIC at ₹1,480 (₹1,758 cr, 28-Aug-2026), taking it to ~32.8% fully diluted. At ₹1,425 Ather is worth ~₹56,447 cr, ~15x its FY26 revenue of ₹3,672 cr (net loss ₹517 cr): a growth valuation that can swing hard. We apply a 20% holding discount (no control, tax on any sale, Hero is a long-term holder), as the street (Motilal Oswal, Emkay) and our own Tata Chemicals report do.

**Hero FinCorp** lends to two-wheeler buyers, MSMEs and individuals (FY26 total income ₹9,583 cr). It lost ₹226 cr in FY26 on high credit costs, paid Hero only ₹6 cr of dividends, and its IPO (approved by SEBI in 2025, ~₹3,668 cr) had not launched by Sep-2026. We value Hero's 40.45% at 1.0x Mar-26 book less 20% (₹95 a share), inside the street's ₹55-215 range; book is generous for a loss-making lender and our bear case uses 0.7x.

blocks.callout: **So what:** at ₹5,241 the market pays ₹4,373 a share for Hero's own business once the stakes are counted, ~13.3x our FY28E EPS. That is the main reason we see value. But note that our core multiple comes from Hero's own price history, and that price always included some value for these stakes: if history is adjusted for them, the core multiple would be lower (see Valuation). Ather alone is ~₹734 of our target, so a 30% fall in Ather's price would cut our target by ~₹220.

sections.title: Net cash of ~₹15,400 cr plus ~₹3,900 cr of stakes at book; suppliers fund the working capital

blocks.p: At Mar-2026 Hero held ₹767 cr of cash and ₹19,286 cr of investments, of which ₹3,901 cr were its associates at book value (Hero FinCorp ₹2,407 cr, Ather ₹1,093 cr, Euler ₹401 cr) and ~₹400 cr other strategic holdings. Borrowings were ₹779 cr (₹280 cr leases, ₹499 cr working-capital loans in the Colombia and Bangladesh subsidiaries). Net treasury excluding the stakes was ~₹15,400 cr, about ₹765 a share. Working capital is negative: suppliers are paid in ~88 days while dealers pay in ~18 and inventory turns in ~31, so growth releases cash (FY26 working-capital inflow ₹2,375 cr).

blocks.p: Nine houses published after the Q1FY27 results (7-11 Aug 2026). Buy/Add/Outperform: Motilal Oswal ₹6,560, Emkay ₹6,700, Choice ₹6,450, Citi ₹6,670, JPMorgan ₹6,845, CLSA ₹6,555. The median is ₹6,555 (average ₹6,323), set when the stock was ₹5,550-5,790; by 30-Sep-2026 it had fallen to ₹5,241, so the same targets imply ~25% upside. sections.title: Valuation: 15x core earnings plus ₹868 of stakes gives {{dcf.tp|inr}}

blocks.h: Method: the street's, on our numbers

blocks.p: We value Hero the way the street does: **P/E on core earnings plus the stakes**. Core earnings = our consolidated EPS before the share of associates, for the twelve months the market will look at in September 2027 (Sep-28E: half FY28E, half FY29E) = ₹349.4. The stakes are valued separately (previous chapter). Because the engine has no "plus stakes" line, the P/E line in our model and Excel carries a **composite multiple** of 17.5x = 15x + ₹868 ÷ ₹349.4 (bull 20.5x, bear 15.0x); it is arithmetic, not a view that Hero deserves 17.5x.

sections.title: Our honest summary: cheap for a reason, but cheap; BUY with a thin margin of safety

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** the world's largest two-wheeler maker with a near-monopoly in India's 100-110cc motorcycles, ~₹15,400 cr of net cash, 35% ROCE, negative working capital, a 70% payout, a fast-growing parts business, credible share gains in scooters and EVs, and ~₹868 a share of stakes (mostly Ather).

**What you are paying:** ₹5,241, i.e. 15.9x our FY28E EPS, or ~13.3x for the core once the stakes are counted, for ~9% EPS growth in a home segment that keeps losing share of the market. On the street's method and our inputs the target is {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): BUY, but only just; a history adjusted for the stakes would make it a HOLD.

Internal-combustion (petrol) engine vehicles / battery-electric vehicles. VIDA is Hero's EV brand.
Dispatches are vehicles shipped from factories to dealers (SIAM data); retail is vehicles registered by buyers, from the government VAHAN database.
Net revenue per unit, after GST and dealer margin. Rises with price increases and a richer mix.
Goods and Services Tax on two-wheelers up to 350cc cut from 28% to 18% from 22-Sep-2025; above 350cc moved to 40%.
Production Linked Incentive: a government subsidy on qualifying locally made EVs, booked as income (~13% of EV revenue for Hero once the whole range qualifies).

A company in which Hero has significant influence but not control (Hero FinCorp, Ather, Euler). Hero carries it at cost plus its share of profits, and books its share of profit or loss in one P&L line.
An accounting gain when an associate issues new shares at a price above Hero's carrying value, even though Hero sells nothing (₹722 cr in Q1FY26 on Ather's IPO and a private placement).
A discount to the market value of a stake held by another company, reflecting lack of control, tax on a sale and the fact that the parent may never sell.
Rights to buy new shares later at a fixed price; Hero paid 25% upfront for 76.19 lakh Ather warrants at ₹1,260 and pays the rest on conversion within 18 months.
Here: consolidated earnings per share before the share of associates and one-off items.
The P/E used in our model: core multiple plus the stakes per share divided by Sep-28E EPS (an engine workaround; see Valuation).
Half of FY28E plus half of FY29E: the 12-month-forward earnings the market will look at in September 2027.
Share price ÷ earnings per share; enterprise value (market value less net cash) ÷ EBITDA.
Discounted cash flow valuation; WACC is the required annual return used to discount future cash (here the cost of equity, as Hero has net cash).
Long-period average of monsoon rainfall (~87 cm for June-September).

statementNotes.sales@FY20: −14%: slowdown before the BS6 emission switch (Apr-2020) and Covid in March.
statementNotes.sales@FY22: −5%: Covid second wave, rural stress and BS6-led price increases hit commuter demand.
statementNotes.ebitdaMargin@FY22: Down to 11.0%: steel, aluminium and other input costs spiked faster than prices.
statementNotes.ebitdaMargin@FY24: Up to 13.9%: input deflation, price increases and better mix.
statementNotes.pat@FY24: +34%: margin recovery; includes ₹160 cr VRS charge and −₹120 cr share of associates (mainly Ather losses).
statementNotes.sales@FY26: +16%: volume +9.6% to 64.69 lakh after the GST cut (22-Sep-2025); scooters +46%, exports +39%.
statementNotes.ebitdaMargin@FY26: 14.9%: ICE margin 17.0% (pricing, LEAP savings, operating leverage) less ~2.3 pts of VIDA losses.
statementNotes.otherIncome@FY26: Screener basis: other income ₹1,058 cr + share of associates ₹385 cr (incl. ₹722 cr dilution gain) − ₹119 cr labour-code exceptional.
statementNotes.pat@FY26: +32% reported; +~25% before associates and one-offs (EPS ~₹283 vs ₹287 reported).
statementNotes.cfo@FY26: +94% to ₹8,315 cr: payables +₹1,977 cr and receivables −₹1,027 cr (working-capital inflow ₹2,375 cr).
statementNotes.sales@Q2FY26: +17%: GST cut from 22-Sep-2025 and festive restocking; volumes +11%.
statementNotes.sales@Q4FY26: +30%: record quarter; volumes +24% on the post-GST surge.
statementNotes.pat@Q1FY26: +65%: includes ~₹722 cr one-time gain on dilution of associates (Ather IPO, private placement).
statementNotes.otherIncome@Q1FY26: Screener includes the share of associates (+₹629 cr, mostly the dilution gain).
statementNotes.sales@Q1FY27: +35%: volume +23%, mix +8% (scooters, VIDA, premium, exports, parts), ~4.5% price increases.
statementNotes.opm@Q1FY27: 13%: gross margin −300 bp QoQ on ~4.5% commodity inflation (West Asia); other expenses −14% QoQ.
statementNotes.pat@Q1FY27: −17% vs a base with the ₹722 cr gain; standalone +29%. Associates −₹44 cr.
statementNotes.otherIncome@Q1FY27: ₹460 cr (+48%): higher treasury income; breakdown not disclosed.
statementNotes.sales@FY27E: GAM: volume +8.6% (H1 strong, Sep-Mar ~+3.5% on the post-GST base and a weak monsoon), revenue per vehicle +7.4% (price ~5%, mix, parts +20%).
statementNotes.ebitdaMargin@FY27E: GAM: Q1's 13.3% improves modestly as price increases and cost cuts offset commodities; VIDA losses ~₹900 cr.
statementNotes.otherIncome@FY27E: GAM: 8.5% yield on earning treasury; no yield on stakes (incl. ₹2,000 cr into Ather in Aug-26); associates excluded.
statementNotes.pat@FY27E: GAM: before associates; flat on reported FY26 (which had the ₹722 cr gain), ~+2% on FY26 before associates and one-offs.
statementNotes.ebitdaMargin@FY28E: GAM: back into the 14-16% band as VIDA scales with PLI and commodities normalise.
